explanation:
[EFFECT] Wind speed has a mostly one-directional, downward effect on predicted bike demand: at calm conditions (near 0 km/h) the contribution is close to neutral or very slightly positive, but as wind speed rises above roughly 20 km/h, the model progressively reduces its demand forecast. At the highest recorded wind speeds (~55–60 km/h), the suppression becomes quite strong (SHAP values around −0.4 to −0.7 in log space), meaning the model predicts meaningfully fewer rentals in very windy hours.

[IMPORTANCE] Windspeed is the 8th most important feature out of 9, with an importance score of 0.020. It has a relatively minor overall influence on demand compared to features like hour of day or temperature, though it can matter noticeably at extreme wind levels.

[RECOMMENDATION] During forecasted high-wind periods (above roughly 20–30 km/h), slightly reducing the number of bikes deployed at exposed or open stations can help avoid overstocking, as demand is likely to be lower than on calm days.
